analysis:
Reviewed the primary analysis against the replayed workflow, builder patch, changelog and documentation. No independently supported security regression was identified. The replay is incomplete (11 source units omitted), so this conclusion does not clear the entire release path.

.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml:37-203 pins actions, checks tag/version and published CLI compatibility, imports a team-selected signing identity, notarizes, verifies and publishes desktop artifacts. desktop-app/electron-builder.ts:20-34 adds release credential/team checks and mandatory signing; lines 53-68 enable release notarization and validated signing. These controls concern distribution identity, not provider serving permission. Nothing supplied changes the coordinator's authorization, endpoint custody, encryption, cache isolation, billing or fan authority. A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054 and TB-011 remain relevant: signing/notarization must not substitute for exact provider-artifact qualification.

Remaining material review concerns the new signing/distribution path. The workflow executes npm ci and dist with the shared signing identity available (84-130), but the complete packaging scripts and artifact contents are not replayed. Verify that the published DMG/ZIP contain the exact app assessed at 160-175; ZIP existence and hashing do not independently establish that correspondence. Signing cleanup at 205-208 depends on KEYCHAIN_PATH being exported at 117, after import and identity resolution; failure-path credential retention depends on runner isolation, which is not supplied. These are unresolved contracts, not established exploits.

The manual-dispatch dry-run claim in the workflow and changelog is inconsistent with ref-only publication selection at workflow:51-56: dispatch on an unpublished matching tag can publish. No supplied evidence establishes an adversarial authorization bypass, so this is not reported as a security finding. Human review should reconcile that publication intent and the unresolved artifact/credential-lifecycle contracts before public distribution.
